title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: quia paruisti — words personal to Adam, not to us immediately
pass_a_gloss: So what? Are 'because you obeyed your wife's voice' meant as addressed to you—to your person—and aimed at you right away? See how personal that was, how proper to Adam as Eve's husband, how those words fit his person. Could the divine sentence have been cast in speech more personal to Adam, more his own, less shared with humankind?
pass_b_english: What then? Do you think those words—because you obeyed your wife's voice—were spoken to you, to your person, I say, and look to you immediately? Do you not see how personal it was, and proper to Adam, that he was Eve's husband, how fitted to his person these words are? Could God's sentence have been conceived in words more, so to speak, personal, more proper to Adam's person, less common to the human race?
source_text: Quid enim? putasne ista verba, quia paruisti voci uxoris tuae, tibi, tuae, inquam, personae dicta esse, & ad te immediate spectare? Nonne vides quam personale fuit, & proprium Adamo, maritum fuisse Evae, tam ad eius personam accommodata esse haec verba? Potuitne Dei sententia verbis concipi magis, ut ita loquar, personalibus, magis propriis personae Adami, minus communibus generi humano?
